status_text: All 16 new task arrivals, zero falls; laptop closure still 0/4. No additional Tinker controller training has run.
diagnosis: Previously recorded pelvis paths were about 2.0–2.1 m for roughly 1.1 m of waypoints. The controller aligned to the final task direction up to 70 mm early, then shuffled. A first new follower also switched out of final alignment and drifted during stopping. Those failed calibration trials were retained.
storage_text: The live inventory found 100 checkpoints, at the organization’s free checkpoint-count limit. Six are Mochi full training states. Nothing was deleted and billing was not changed. Four new full states need about 1.75 GB and four checkpoint slots.
provenance_text: 9 new Modal rollouts in this paired-route study, plus 80 preceding isolated contact calibrations. Source-verified past.dev handoffs and an Exa search ran in the study. Tinker provided research-decision inference here; no controller post-training ran.
results_note: Calibration scenarios, not reserved tests. The old method includes a fifth transit stop; the new method follows intermediate vertices without that stop. Task-arrival error excludes the old transit stop. The new laptop profile B was chosen for stability after unsuccessful contact calibration; the old fixed baseline uses C. This is a combined engineering comparison. A short failed episode is not more efficient. No comparison of model weights has been performed. On the one case where both methods finished navigation (19003), walking time rose from 47.1 to 52.6 s and pelvis path from 2.123 to 2.255 m. Improved precision and visual clearance came with a speed/distance cost. The maximum measured tracking errors exceed the assumed 5 mm allowance.
